new_statements.rule_in_words: Mabaan is a tone language (Andersen 1992 per LLBA abstract: two underlying tones, high and low; PHOIBLE lists H, L and contour tones). The only accessible statement on stress is Storch's survey remark that in the Burun subgroup (which includes Mabaan) stress has no grammatical or lexical function and the stress-tone interface plays no significant role. No source opened states where word stress falls; the 2006 Mabaan-English dictionary marks stress on individual entries (e.g. locative -jI stressed vs -ji unstressed, 'stress on last syllable of beedi') without a general rule.
new_statements.exceptions: None stated; the dictionary's entry notes imply stress can distinguish suffix readings (stressed vs unstressed -ji), which sits uneasily with Storch's 'no lexical function' and is unresolved.
new_statements.domain_note: Storch's statement is a subgroup-level survey claim (Burun), reconstructed from Internet Archive search snippets of an access-restricted book, not from an opened page; the Mabaan-specific primary description (Andersen 1992) was not opened. Word level; no phrase-level discussion seen.
new_statements.identity_note: Glottolog maba1273 'Mabaan' = ISO mfz = Southern Burun (Wikipedia's article title); also spelled Maban/Meban, not to be confused with the Maban family of Chad (maba1277 etc.). Storch's statement covers the Burun subgroup as a whole (Northern Burun = Mayak, mayk1239; Southern Burun = Mabaan, Ulu, Jumjum jumj1238); it is not Mabaan-specific.

sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: No introduction or phonology section. Scattered entry-level notes distinguish stress from tone, e.g. locative suffix '-ji' glossed '(stress on -jI)' vs '(unstressed -ji)', 'Note stress on last syl. of beedi', 'gokce 3sg stem unstressed'; tones noted per entry (low/high/hl). No general rule for word-stress placement.
